_README: Reconciled facts for turkeyforamericans (3-AI panel: claude+deepseek+grok). The ONLY facts file in the repo. serve_live values never frozen. verify_recommended = confirm against official source before relying. Stage 3 reads this + corrections.json.

locale.money_framing: express costs in USD with Turkish lira (TRY) equivalents

power_plug_voltage.value: 230V / 50Hz, Type C and Type F (European round-pin). Americans need a plug adapter; most phone/laptop chargers are dual-voltage, but 120V-only devices need a converter.

visa._note: YMYL. RULING: US ordinary-passport tourists are visa-free (2-of-3 panel; reflects the ~2020 change). grok's e-visa answer reflects pre-2020 rules. Confirm at evisa.gov.tr before relying.

passport_validity_required.value: Passport valid at least 150 days beyond date of entry, with a blank page
passport_validity_required.notes: RULING: state Turkey's specific 150-day rule (stricter/more precise than the generic 6-month default two models gave). Following 150 days also satisfies 6 months.

notes.value: Carry proof of accommodation and return travel; rarely checked but officially expected.

approx_rate_note.notes: VOLATILE — lira depreciates persistently; never freeze a USD/TRY rate. Serve live.

cash_vs_card.value: Cards widely accepted in cities, hotels, and tourist areas; carry some cash for markets, taxis, small towns, tips, and rural areas

atm_availability.value: ATMs plentiful in cities and tourist towns. Decline the ATM's offered conversion (choose to be charged in TRY, not USD) to avoid bad DCC rates. Watch for high fees on some bank ATMs.

currency_import_export_limit.notes: RULING: sources disagreed ($5k vs $10k vs 25,000 TRY export) — left null pending official confirmation. See _open_questions.

tipping_norm.value: Tipping (bahşiş) is customary but modest: ~5-10% in restaurants if service not included, round up taxis, small tips for hotel staff and hammam attendants. Less aggressive than US tipping culture.

intercity_rail.value: High-speed rail (YHT) connects Istanbul–Ankara–Konya and Ankara–Sivas; useful but network is limited. Most intercity travel is by plane or bus, not train.

buses.value: Extensive, comfortable, and cheap intercity bus network (otobüs) — companies like Metro, Kamil Koç, Pamukkale. Long distances (e.g. Istanbul–Cappadocia ~11h overnight) make flying often preferable.

domestic_flights.value: Cheap, frequent domestic flights are the backbone of multi-region trips. Turkish Airlines, AnadoluJet/AJet, Pegasus. Key routes: IST–Kayseri/Nevşehir (for Cappadocia), IST–Antalya, IST–Izmir, IST–Dalaman.

ride_sharing.value: BiTaksi and iTaksi apps hail licensed taxis in Istanbul; Uber operates in Istanbul but dispatches yellow taxis. Always insist on the meter ('taksimetre'). Trams, metro, ferries, and the Istanbulkart make Istanbul easy without taxis.

car_rental_and_driving.value: Drive on the RIGHT (same as US). US license accepted for short visits but an International Driving Permit (IDP) is recommended/sometimes required. Driving is aggressive in cities; renting makes sense for the coast/Cappadocia, not Istanbul. BAC limit 0.05% (0.00% if towing).

climate_by_season.value: Spring (Apr-May) and fall (Sep-Oct) are ideal nearly everywhere: warm, dry, fewer crowds. Summer (Jun-Aug) is hot — great for coast/beaches, brutal for sightseeing in Istanbul and harsh in the interior. Winter is cold inland (Cappadocia can snow — atmospheric for balloons) and mild but rainy on the coast. Istanbul winters are gray and chilly.

safety_health._note: YMYL. Advisory change-prone + partly regional (SE Syria border). Confirm at travel.state.gov before relying.

advisory_level.value: US State Dept ~Level 2 ('Exercise Increased Caution') in most areas, with higher do-not-travel warnings near the Syria border and Şırnak/Hakkari provinces
advisory_level.notes: Tourist regions (Istanbul, Cappadocia, coast) are not the high-warning zones. Confirm current level + date.

main_risk.value: Petty theft/pickpocketing in crowded tourist areas (Istanbul transit, bazaars), tourist-targeted scams, occasional anti-government demonstrations (avoid protests), and earthquake risk (Turkey is seismically active; major Feb 2023 quake affected the southeast, NOT the western tourist regions)

vaccines.value: No vaccines required for entry from the US. Keep routine vaccines current; CDC sometimes recommends Hepatitis A and typhoid for some travelers — check cdc.gov.
vaccines.notes: RULING: conservative 'none required, check CDC' framing.

tap_water_safe.value: Tap water is chlorinated and generally considered safe in major cities but is heavily mineralized and not pleasant-tasting; nearly everyone (locals included) drinks cheap bottled water. Stick to bottled to avoid stomach upset.

emergency_numbers.notes: 112 is the unified emergency number (works for medical); Jandarma (rural) 156.

sim_esim.value: eSIM is the easiest option for Americans (Airalo, Holafly, etc.) — install before arrival. Physical Turkish SIMs (Turkcell, Vodafone, Türk Telekom) require passport registration; phones used >120 days must be IMEI-registered (a tax) or get blocked, but short tourist visits are fine.

coverage.value: Excellent 4G/5G in cities and tourist regions; good even in Cappadocia and along the coast. Patchy in remote eastern mountains.

costs._note: serve_live ranges; Turkey is cheap for Americans (lira weakness) but high local inflation moves lira prices constantly.

daily_budget_mid.value: ~$100-180/day (good 3-4 star, restaurants, some tours, domestic flights)

daily_budget_high.value: ~$300+/day (cave suites, luxury Bosphorus hotels, private guides)

dress_norms.value: Turkey is secular and Western-dressed in cities and resorts — normal Western clothing is fine. For MOSQUES: women cover hair (scarf), shoulders, and knees; men wear long pants; shoes off. Carry a scarf when mosque-visiting. More conservative dress respected in rural/eastern areas.

how_to_get_there.value: Primary US gateway — nonstop Turkish Airlines/United from JFK, EWR, IAD, ORD, LAX, SFO, IAH, MIA (seasonal). Arrive at Istanbul Airport (IST).

local_transport.value: Get an Istanbulkart (rechargeable transit card) — works on metro, tram, ferries, funiculars, buses. The T1 tram serves Sultanahmet (old city). Ferries across the Bosphorus are scenic and cheap. Walkable historic core.

airport.value: Istanbul Airport (IST), ~28 mi NW of city center on the European side. Havaist airport buses, M11 metro, or taxi (~45-90 min depending on traffic). Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) is on the Asian side — cheaper flights but far from Sultanahmet.

Passport validity: confirm Turkey's 150-days-beyond-entry rule officially (panel gave 150 days vs generic 6 months).
Currency declaration limit: UNRESOLVED — sources gave $5,000 / $10,000 / 25,000 TRY export. Left null; verify before printing any number.
